items.title: Anthropic widens its Cyber Verification Program to three access tiers
items.blurb: Vetted security teams can now get stronger cyber capabilities and fewer blocking classifiers on Claude, on Anthropic's own platform as well as through Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry.

items.title: Claude opens up for verified pen testers and red teams
items.blurb: Under the expanded program, verified defenders get tiered access with relaxed safety limits for red-teaming, incident response and work on critical infrastructure.

items.title: Eight flawed intermediate certificates put the web on alert
items.blurb: Researchers found eight defective intermediate TLS certificates issued by the Indian certificate authority eMudhra, with a flaw engineers had considered impossible; browsers and CAs are moving to revoke them.

items.title: eMudhra certificate flaw forces emergency revocations
items.blurb: Eight intermediate certificates from eMudhra were found broken in a way that could let attackers impersonate websites; admins are told to check which chains their services rely on.

items.title: Gemini 4 Argon ships with 30% fewer bad commits
items.blurb: Google says its new model lifts agent coding output by about a third and cuts the bugs that slip through code review by 30%, with completions of up to one million tokens.

items.title: How Long Decode lets Gemini 4 Argon write a million tokens
items.blurb: Google's developer guide explains Long Decode, which spreads one very long completion across several model calls, and the model is broadly available at a discounted $2/$10 per million tokens for now.

items.title: Meta open-sources an 816B model aimed at coding agents
items.blurb: Muse Spark Open activates 42 billion of its 816 billion parameters per request, reads up to a million tokens of context and is built for long agentic coding tasks.

items.title: Muse Spark Open becomes the strongest US open-weights model
items.blurb: Meta's new release runs locally on two linked Mac Studio desktops, putting a frontier-class open model on hardware a small team can buy.

items.title: Anthropic drops Git for an in-house version control system
items.blurb: After Claude-driven development pushed daily merges from about 2,500 to more than 30,000, Anthropic built Scion, a server-centric system, to keep its monorepo fast.

items.title: Inside Scion, the source control behind 30,000 merges a day
items.blurb: Anthropic describes why Git stopped scaling for its monorepo and how it migrated to Scion without pausing development.

items.title: Scion cuts CI checkouts from minutes to seconds
items.blurb: Anthropic reports that its new version control uses 200 times less CPU and memory than the Git setup it replaced.

items.title: OpenAI tunes its model for COBOL, Fortran and Visual Basic
items.blurb: OpenAI updated its flagship model to help companies modernize decades-old business software written in legacy languages.

items.title: GPT-6.1 Sol jumps to 86.6% on COBOL migration
items.blurb: New evaluations across 20 programming languages show the model migrating COBOL correctly 86.6% of the time at low reasoning effort, up from 5.4% for the previous generation.

items.title: Claude designs 300,000 proteins against scorpion venom
items.blurb: Working largely on its own, Claude generated and ranked candidate binders; 17 of the 211 designs tested in the lab met strict binding criteria.

items.title: AI-designed mini-binders take a first step toward toxin research
items.blurb: Anthropic stresses that the promising designs are an early research result, not a working antivenom.

items.title: Anthropic's free scanner flags 77 critical bugs in open source
items.blurb: In its first week, the AI-based OSS Scanner reported 77 critical and 803 high-severity vulnerabilities to project maintainers.

items.title: Cisco email gateway zero-day under active attack again
items.blurb: A critical path traversal flaw lets unauthenticated attackers write files and run commands as root on Secure Email Gateway appliances with File Reputation enabled.

items.title: Google warns of China-linked attacks on a BeyondTrust flaw
items.blurb: Google expects wider exploitation of a Remote Support vulnerability; hosted customers are patched, self-hosted ones should update now.

items.title: Microsoft treats AI agents like potential insider threats
items.blurb: New Guardian Agents and agent detection in Defender monitor AI agents independently, on the premise that frontier models can't simply be trusted.

items.title: Why CVE tracking misses most AI agent risks
items.blurb: A security researcher argues that agent permissions, prompt injection, shared identities and tool chains need tracking that CVE numbers alone don't give.

items.title: Attackers breach an old OpenCode system and run up AI bills
items.blurb: The coding tool says 1.4% of Console users were affected after attackers got into a legacy system and charged usage to their AI accounts.

items.title: PHP prepares emergency patches for two critical flaws
items.blurb: Two remote code execution bugs are thought to affect PHP 5 through 8; maintainers have announced fixes for the next day.

items.title: Claude Haiku 5.5 brings frontier speed at a quarter of the price
items.blurb: Anthropic's new small model costs $0.10 per million input tokens below 100,000 tokens and supports a one-million-token context window.

items.title: DeepSeek releases a faster open Flash model with free search
items.blurb: V4.1-Flash is trained with reinforcement learning from self-feedback and ships alongside public Search and Fetch APIs.

items.title: LiquidAI fits a 24B reasoning model on the device
items.blurb: The new model keeps only 2 billion parameters active at a time, so reasoning runs locally on laptops and phones.

items.title: Fish Audio's Drama 3 voice model takes stage directions
items.blurb: The open-weight text-to-speech model follows plain-English directions and controls emotion and pacing word by word, and can be self-hosted.

items.title: NVIDIA open-sources a voice model that talks while it listens
items.blurb: PersonaPlex-7B handles full-duplex conversation with low latency on a single GPU.

items.title: Z.ai's GLM-Legal rivals frontier models on legal work
items.blurb: The specialised model targets end-to-end legal workflows at a fraction of the per-task cost of general frontier models.

items.title: Black Forest Labs releases a 5.6B open image model
items.blurb: The open-weights model handles text-to-image generation and editing with several reference images.

items.title: GPT-6 turns ChatGPT answers into interactive mini apps
items.blurb: With Intelligent UI, ChatGPT can answer with live diagrams, calculators, buttons and forms instead of plain text.

items.title: Claude managed agents coordinate up to 1,000 agents per run
items.blurb: Anthropic's new orchestration runs huge parallel jobs such as codebase-wide bug hunts.

items.title: Anthropic's IPO filing shows steep growth and huge compute bills
items.blurb: The draft prospectus pairs fast revenue growth with an $80 billion-plus loss in the first half and plans for up to $750 billion in compute.

items.title: Microsoft to pay Anthropic $2B a year for Claude in Copilot
items.blurb: Copilot will rely on Claude models for much of its work while sending some workloads to OpenAI to keep costs down.

items.title: Waymo plans to grow its robotaxi fleet fivefold
items.blurb: Backed by a fresh $5 billion, Waymo aims for 20,000 vehicles by the end of next year.

items.title: Meta and Sierra propose an open protocol for personal agents
items.blurb: The Personal Agent Protocol, backed by Shopify, Stripe and Walmart among others, defines how personal AI agents authenticate with businesses.

items.title: Google Labs lets anyone build games by describing them
items.blurb: Playground, a US-only experiment, turns natural-language descriptions into playable games without code or a game engine.

items.title: Apple unveils HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home
items.blurb: The seven-inch device recognises household members and personalises what it shows; it ships on November 13.
